articles.title: It's not AI anymore, it's ‘super intelligence’ (according to the White House) | TechCrunch
articles.summary: [jwp-video] This week, the White House got nearly every major tech CEO in one room — Zuckerberg, Bezos, Musk, and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei among them — to sign an AI safety pledge that President Donald Trump called “morally binding.” Trump also signed an executive order officially rebranding AI as “super intelligence,” and meanwhile, Meta and OpenAI are putting friendlier faces on their AI products, even as the biggest money in AI still appears to be coming from the enterprise.  On this episode of TechCrunch's Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Anthony Ha, and Sean O’Kane dig into this week’s AI moves, the ugly economics of consumer AI, plus the shifting IPO market and a handful of startup deals.  And speaking of startups, join us at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, where Equity will kick things off with a live show on the Builders Stage at 9 a.m. Get 25% off your tickets with code Equity25. articles.title: Musk’s biggest loyalist became his biggest liability
articles.summary: Shivon Zilis is a former OpenAI board member and the mother of several of Musk’s children. Her notes might be the most important evidence we’ve seen so far.
articles.body: I sat down in the Musk v. Altman trial courtroom today, painfully aware that no one was going to ask Shivon Zilis the question on everyone’s minds: Girl, what the fuck are you doing? Zilis, who testified under oath that she is the mother of four of Musk’s children, was… What’s the best way to characterize this? A Musk adviser? She denies she was a “chief of staff” but says she worked for Musk’s “entire AI portfolio: Tesla, Neuralink, and OpenAI” starting in 2017. The two met through OpenAI, and they had what she referred to as a “one off” before becoming “friends and colleagues.” The “one off,” she confirmed, was “romantic in nature.” Her job under Musk was “to go find bottlenecks and solve them,” and she claims to have worked 80 to 100 hours a week doing that. “It was just bananas,” she said. Her first two children by Musk — twins — were born in 2021, while Zilis was serving on OpenAI’s board. She kept this a secret. She did not tell the board who the father was until Business Insider reported on court documents that listed Musk as the father. “My first call was to my dad,” said Zilis, who testified that even her own family didn’t know the children’s paternity. “The call right after that was to Sam Altman.” Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president, had testified he found out about Zilis’ children from news reports. When he talked to her about it, she claimed her relationship with Musk was “platonic” and that she’d had kids via IVF. This was reassurance enough for Brockman, who’d been friends with her since 2013. She remained on the board. On the stand, Zilis spoke softly and quickly. She seemed mousy. A significant part of what made her testimony so bad for Musk was that she appeared to be the only person taking notes on what Brockman, Altman, Ilya Sutskever, and Musk were discussing when the cofounders considered their options for creating a for-profit arm of OpenAI. She also was “aiding and facilitating communication between the principal parties.” Those notes are the trial’s most important evidence — more important, even, than Brockman’s diary. The goal of the direct testimony seemed to be to take the sting out of what Zilis and the plaintiff’s lawyers had to know was coming. So she told the court that her role also meant telling Altman when Musk was “in a good headspace” for a conversation — perhaps inadvertently strengthening Brockman’s testimony Tuesday that at one point he feared Musk would physically attack him — while vehemently denying that she funneled information to Musk. It didn’t work. Look, she and Musk testified they lived together and have a romantic relationship and four kids. She was originally a plaintiff in the suit. She kept her children’s paternity secret from her own father. All of those things would be reason enough to doubt her testimony about thinking OpenAI betrayed its mission during the chaos when Altman was fired by the board. She claimed that Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said something to the effect of “we are above them, we are below them, we are around them” and described that chaotic period as being “terrifying.” (The quote was “We are below them, above them, around them.”) But the notes are really what did Musk’s case in. Try as she might, Zilis couldn’t explain them away. There were a lot of ideas batted around in 2017 and 2018. We saw a lot of Zilis’ emails from that period. Notably in one, an option was “switch to for profit in next couple of weeks (woah fast!).” Another email noted that a “complete non-negotiable” for Altman, Brockman, and Sutskever “is an ironclad agreement to not have Elon (or anyone) have absolutely [sic] control of AGI they create.” In another she wrote to Musk money manager Jared Birchall, “They say they will not move forward without a guarantee to switch away from him having control. You and I can argue that’s stupid all we want but they are holding firm on it.” Zilis also knew about Musk halting donations before OpenAI did. On August 20th, 2017, she wrote, “Funding freeze: OpenAI is likely to realize this week that their $5M in Q3 is, albeit correctly, on hold. Unsure how this will impact negotiations but wanted to flag it since it’s likely to have a big psychological impact on them if they find out.” Musk told Brockman and Sutskever over a week later, on September 1st, that he’d pulled funding. There were other machinations: * At one point, Musk seemed to have suggested that she, Sam Teller, and Birchall — two of Musk’s closest fixers — should all take seats on OpenAI’s board so that Musk would have control of the nonprofit. Zilis wrote to Teller that she didn’t share that with the OpenAI team. * In November 2017, Musk was thinking of creating a “world-class AI lab” inside Tesla. To that end, Musk offered Altman a board seat at Tesla. * Zilis wrote an email to Musk saying that to save him time she’d brainstormed some solutions for him. Three of them involved developing AGI at Tesla. One was making OpenAI a public benefit corporation subsidiary of Tesla. One was getting Altman as an “anchor” for TeslaAI. * My favorite of those solutions was: “Find a way to get Demis. Seriously…. Demis really does fanboy hard and I don’t think he’s immoral… just amoral. If he hung around E perhaps it would force him to think about humanity more.” * After hiring Andrej Karpathy, Musk asked for a list of top OpenAI people to poach. We had already seen one of her text messages in the docket — the one where Musk leaves the board and she asks him whether she should remain “close and friendly” to continue funneling him information. In her direct testimony, she tried to put that in context: “They were going through this weird half-breakup,” she said. But in the cross, we found out that she didn’t remember that in her deposition. “Your long-lost memories have been recovered,” said Sarah Eddy, the OpenAI attorney, in one of the trial’s funnier moments. Sure, Musk’s team objected and the objection was sustained, but we all heard it. In fact, it was one of several times Zilis seemed to have recovered memories she didn’t have at her deposition, memories that — coincidentally I’m sure — happened to be good for Musk’s case. To be fair, Zilis performed the best under cross-examination of anyone we’ve seen so far, but she doesn’t exactly come across as truthful. And there was even more reason to be skeptical of her when we discovered how she left the board, which — according to her deposition — happened “because I picked up a call from Sam and he said, ‘I’ve heard Elon is starting a competitive venture’ and I said, ‘Well if that’s true, this is the time to resign.’” Mysteriously, she had forgotten that call between the deposition and today. But she did seem to know that Musk was moving on AI when she texted a friend, who was in her phone as “Shahini Rubicon Fluffer.” (Incredible name. Thomas Pynchon will be so jealous.) “Have to resign OpenAI board btw,” she wrote. “E’s effort has become well-known.” Her friend didn’t seem surprised by the revelation. Zilis went on: “When the father of your babies starts a competitive effort and will recruit out of OpenAI there is nothing to be done.” Zilis added that Musk “proactively apologized that he had pruned my friend network through this.” Here’s what it added up to, as far as I am concerned: Her primary allegiance was and is to Musk. To believe she didn’t know about xAI, I would have to believe that despite their — at the time — three children and the time he spent with them every week, he never discussed it with her. I don’t believe that. Who would? There’s enough evidence in her meeting notes to suggest she routinely held back information from OpenAI on Musk’s behalf — xAI would be no different. I also don’t believe that she didn’t give Musk information about the Microsoft deals she approved while sitting on OpenAI’s board. Musk didn’t have a problem converting the whole of OpenAI to a for-profit or kneecapping the charity by recruiting its strongest researchers. He didn’t mind the idea of subsuming it into Tesla in any of a variety of ways. The thing he did mind was not being in control of it. That’s what I took away from Zilis’ texts and emails. Brockman and the OpenAI board were incredibly naive to allow Zilis to continue working there after learning of her twins’ paternity. But then, maybe no one expected someone so meek to be so devious. She was smart enough not to raise her voice or nitpick obvious questions during her cross-examination, so her bearing read as more trustworthy than anyone we’ve seen yet. It’s just that the overall takeaway from her written communications is that she’s put Musk first in her life. Everyone else — including, apparently, her own father — comes second. So on the stand, you might as well assume she’s saying what Musk wants to hear too.

articles.title: Thieves stole an Nvidia-branded truck filled with just 20,000 pounds of sand—and it points to Big Tech’s $150 million AI hardware theft headache
articles.summary: While the thieves left the sand-filled trailer unscathed, other freighters have faced real threats from organized criminals in search of high-value data cent...
articles.body:
Cargo pirates, perhaps in search of precious AI loot, found a completely different kind of booty after stealing two trailers from an autonomous trucking company: sand, and lots of it.

The trucking company, PlusAI, confirmed two trailers were stolen last week from its Fremont, Calif., warehouse, including one with Nvidia branding on it. While PlusAI uses Nvidia chips for its self-driving technology, the trailers weren't carrying those chips, but rather, 40,000 pounds of sand.

The theft happened overnight: Workers discovered the trailers missing the next morning, and police recovered them later that day after a friend of PlusAI's vice president of legal happened to spot them parked outside a Newark office and sent a photo. Authorities told the company the thieves broke open the back of the vehicles, found nothing of value, and left them.

PlusAI uses sand to simulate the loads its trailers must carry to support research and development testing, as carrying the material closely mimics real freight conditions. Each truck held about 20,000 pounds of sand.

Lauren Kwan, vice president of marketing at PlusAI, told Fortune that since the company's 2016 founding, it has never had a tractor or trailer stolen: "This was a first." Nvidia declined Fortune 's request for comment.

While a first for PlusAI, cargo theft targeting AI companies has been on the rise. In June, investigators with the Cook County Sheriff's Office in Illinois recovered two trailers outside of Chicago, including one containing $300,000 worth of copper wire stolen from Alabama and $1 million in data center equipment reported stolen in Florida. In December 2024, thieves took more than $7 million worth of Nvidia computer chips from a California warehouse, just one day before it was scheduled to deliver its products to a Supermicro facility in San Jose.

Supply-chain risk management firm Overhaul has already tracked more than $150 million in AI equipment cargo losses since it began tracking the data, and AI-related theft, including data center equipment and chips, has increased 34% since 2024. The total value of goods stolen has increased by more than 110% in the same time period.

Cargo theft has existed for centuries, but with worldwide AI spending projected to reach $2.7 trillion this year by some estimates, thieves have found a new target: hijacking AI-related cargo to resell on the black market, taking advantage of the steep demand for memory chips and infrastructure build-out, according to Overhaul executive vice president David Warrick. The result? Supply-chain chaos for tech and freight companies, and a big payday for thieves.

images.caption: Tech and freight companies are increasingly plagued by AI-related cargo theft. · Fortune · PHILIPPE LOPEZ—AFP/Getty Images

articles.title: Quem é Shivon Zilis, ex-companheira de Elon Musk e executiva da Neuralink | G1
articles.standfirst: Executiva da Neuralink, canadense é formada por Yale e já passou por Tesla e OpenAI; ela e o bilionário tiveram quatro filhos em cinco anos por fertilização in vitro.
articles.summary: Executiva da Neuralink, canadense é formada por Yale e já passou por Tesla e OpenAI; ela e o bilionário tiveram quatro filhos em cinco anos por fertilização in vitro.
articles.body:
Shivon Zilis é executiva na Neuralink. — Foto: Repropdução/X

Shivon Zilis , executiva da Neuralink, empresa de Elon Musk voltada ao desenvolvimento de implantes cerebrais, confirmou nesta sexta-feira (2) o fim de seu relacionamento com o bilionário .

Os dois tiveram quatro filhos em cinco anos , concebidos por fertilização in vitro (FIV), técnica que utiliza óvulos e espermatozoides em laboratório antes de transferir o embrião para o útero.

Nascida no Canadá, Zilis é formada pela Universidade Yale e tem trajetória profissional ligada à inteligência artificial (IA) e ao aprendizado de máquina, área da computação que permite a sistemas identificar padrões e aprender com dados.

Desde 2017, ela atua na Neuralink como diretora de operações e projetos especiais. Antes disso, foi diretora de projetos da Tesla , onde trabalhou em projetos de IA ligados às equipes do Autopilot e de desenvolvimento de chips.

Na OpenAI , foi consultora entre 2016 e 2019 e integrou o conselho da empresa de 2020 a 2023. Zilis também foi integrante do conselho do Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute (Amii) e do Vector Institute, no Canadá, e atuou como sócia da Bloomberg, com foco em investimentos em empresas de inteligência artificial.

No início da carreira, trabalhou na IBM em projetos relacionados a tecnologia financeira, estratégia e serviços bancários.

Seu perfil no X se apresenta com a frase: “Inteligência artificial, inteligência biológica e tudo o que existe entre elas e além. Feita no Canadá”.

Executiva Shivon Zilis diz que seu relacionamento com Elon Musk terminou: 'Vou sentir falta dele' — Foto: Reprodução redes social (X) e Reuters

A relação entre Zilis e Musk começou de maneira diferente de um namoro convencional. Segundo depoimento prestado por ela neste ano em um processo judicial envolvendo Musk e Sam Altman, CEO da OpenAI, os dois tiveram um breve envolvimento romântico em 2016, em um evento corporativo da empresa.

Depois disso, segundo Zilis, eles se tornaram amigos próximos e colegas de trabalho. Mais tarde, quando ela decidiu ter filhos como mãe solo, Musk se ofereceu para ser doador de esperma. A relação evoluiu posteriormente para uma parceria romântica.

O biógrafo Walter Isaacson descreveu Zilis como uma companheira intelectual de Musk , e não como uma parceira romântica convencional.

Os dois tiveram os primeiros filhos, os gêmeos Strider e Azure, em 2021, por fertilização in vitro. Em 2024, nasceu Arcadia, e, em 2025, o casal teve o quarto filho, um menino chamado Seldon Lycurgus.

Ao falar sobre o fim da relação, Zilis destacou justamente a importância que os quatro filhos passaram a ter em sua vida.

“Eu o amei mais do que a própria vida, e ele me ensinou 100 vidas de conhecimento e fez meu cálice transbordar de significado”, escreveu.

Ela acrescentou que, apesar da perda, se sente grata pelos quatro filhos e espera que os dois consigam manter uma boa relação como amigos e coparentes.

articles.title: REP RO KHANNA: US and China can't afford an AI arms race with humanity at stake
articles.summary: A proposed U.S.-China AI treaty outlines five pillars, including a global pause on superintelligence and kill switches for all advanced AI models.
articles.body: America and China do not agree on much. But when it comes to AI, we all lose if we lose control. Last month, as the ranking member of the House Select Committee on China, I convened the first-ever congressional hearing calling for a binding, enforceable, and verifiable U.S.-China AI treaty. I also led every Democrat on the Committee in sending the White House a letter demanding global action to tackle AI risks. Within days, President Trump and General Secretary Xi announced that they would establish a bilateral dialogue on AI. This is an important first step that would not have happened without congressional pressure. But this moment demands more than discussion. At my hearing, some of the world's leading experts on AI called for the U.S. and China to form joint technical working groups with both countries' top scientists. Their mission would be to develop mutually trusted verification technologies that prevent either side from cheating once we sign a U.S.-China AI treaty. This is an easy second step we should take today. ANTHROPIC CEO LIKENS AI FIGHT WITH CHINA TO COLD WAR, SEEKS 'DISARMAMENT NEGOTIATIONS' Critically, we also need to begin envisioning what an actual treaty to save humanity from unchecked AI would look like. The risk that humans will lose control of AI or that misaligned models could unleash biological havoc is increasing every day, and if the world's AI superpowers do not act soon, it may be too late. To address these risks, there are five key pillars of a U.S.-China AI treaty. First, we need a worldwide pause on recursive self-improvement. This is when AI develops AI without human intervention, and it's the most likely path to humanity losing control of this technology entirely. Asking AI to design its own safeguards is like asking the fox to guard the henhouse. MIKE JOHNSON REJECTS AI MORATORIUM OVER CHINA THREAT AS CONSERVATIVE ACTIVIST DEMANDS GUARDRAILS Second, we should impose a global pause on superintelligence. As it has been traditionally defined, superintelligence is AI that exceeds human capabilities across all domains. This could unleash Pandora's box, and neither America nor China is ready for it. Third, we must have kill switches embedded in all advanced models. While scientists disagree about the efficacy of kill switches, they would at least give us a fighting chance if rogue models decided to turn against humanity. AI KILL SWITCH BILL COULD SHUT DOWN ROGUE MODELS Fourth, every AI model should be tested in an air-gapped sandbox prior to release to prevent catastrophic misuse. Whether it's an American model or a Chinese model, criminals, terrorists and even misaligned AI agents shouldn't be able to unleash economically devastating cyberattacks because a frontier lab decided to release a beta version. And fifth, but perhaps most importantly, we need to heed President Reagan's wise words and "trust, but verify." Especially with China, we cannot simply take the CCP at its word. Both governments should agree on verification technologies and inspection regimes that ensure Beijing cannot simply cheat, allowing its labs to race ahead while American labs lag behind. We will also need to build institutions that both sides in a fierce competition can trust, such as an International AI Inspection Agency. BEYOND KILLER ROBOTS: CHINA'S REAL AI THREAT TO AMERICA IS ALREADY HERE, EXPERTS WARN During the Cold War, even as America and the USSR fought fiercely, President Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev recognized that nuclear war would have left both nations worse off. Winning an AI war is like winning a nuclear war. It is catastrophic for civilization. In that same spirit, even as we continue to hold China accountable for its predatory economic practices that harm American workers and its human rights abuses, both countries should be able to rally around the common cause of keeping humans in control of AI. A U.S.-China AI treaty advantages neither America nor China, but rather all of humanity. A global pandemic unleashed by rogue AI wouldn't distinguish between American and Chinese citizens, and neither government benefits if mankind ceases to call the shots. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION A verifiable U.S.-China AI treaty will not happen overnight, but if we do not begin the hard work of negotiating such an agreement soon, humanity will pay a steep price. In the meantime, in addition to forming joint technical working groups with China, we need to get our own house in order. For Congress, this means passing laws that prevent AI companies from putting profit over the collective fate of humanity. For American AI labs, this means investing in safety and strengthening their cybersecurity to prevent China from stealing our edge. If lax cybersecurity allows China to obtain our most advanced model weights illicitly, it not only harms our national security, but it also undermines our strongest leverage in pursuit of a U.S.-China AI treaty. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP When it comes to catastrophic AI risks, it cannot be America versus China or Republicans versus Democrats. The arrival of superintelligence arguably marks a more consequential moment for our species than even the dawn of the Industrial Revolution or the development of the atomic bomb. While the former transformed society and the latter risked its very destruction, the most advanced forms of AI threaten to do both. Let's come together and keep humanity in the driver's seat. CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM REP. RO KHANNA

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV is not a fan of AI-generated art | TechCrunch
articles.summary: "There is an ontological difference, even before an aesthetic one, between art and what a machine can generate through statistical calculation based on millions of images created by others," the pope wrote. "Algorithms lack the spark of humanity."
articles.body:
Critics of AI-generated art have a powerful new ally: His Holiness the Bishop of Rome ( Episcopus Romanus ), Primate of Italy ( Primatus Italiae ), and Supreme Pontiff of the Universal Church ( Summus Pontifex Ecclesiae Universalis ).

In a post on X Friday morning , Pope Leo XIV detailed the spiritual difference between human-generated art and art that is generated by machines, as part of a call to preserve human art from the encroachment of AI.

“In this era of artificial intelligence, it is becoming urgent to distinguish human art from what machines produce,” the Servus Servorum Dei wrote. “There is an ontological difference, even before an aesthetic one, between art and what a machine can generate through statistical calculation based on millions of images created by others. Algorithms lack the spark of humanity.”

Pope Leo XIV gave a more detailed statement on AI in an encyclical letter in May , which emphasized the importance of human dignity in a world of increasing automation.

But that hasn’t stopped AI companies from lobbying the supreme pontiff. According to a recent New York Times report , Anthropic has actively lobbied the Vatican to reconsider its position on non-human consciousness — apparently finding little success.

articles.title: Meta parts ways with Virtue AI
articles.summary: “Unfortunately, the arrangement didn’t work out as planned,” a Meta spokesperson told Semafor.
articles.body:
Meta said it's letting go of employees it hired from AI safety startup Virtue AI four months after they joined the company in June, Meta spokesperson Andy Stone told Semafor, chalking it up to clashing work styles.

The departures show Meta is still shaping its strategy around AI and AI safety amid new calls for regulation in Washington.

"Unfortunately, the arrangement didn't work out as planned," Stone said, adding that Meta Superintelligence Labs remains focused on AI safety, alignment and frontier risk. Virtue, an AI security startup, had previously done work with Anthropic, OpenAI and the Commerce Department's NIST.

Axios reported in June that Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song, and Sanmi Koyejo were joining Meta along with other employees from the startup. The team didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: Breaking up (with Elon Musk) is hard to do
articles.summary: The mother of four of Musk’s children, Shivon Zilis, posted that she and Musk had broken up. She previously testified in the Musk v. Altman trial.
articles.body: In a throwback to MySpace-style internet drama, Shivon Zilis announced that she and the father of her four children, Elon Musk, had broken up on X. To do so, she quote-tweeted a post from “Big Tech Alert,” an account that, among other things, monitors what accounts are following and unfollowing each other. That post noted Musk was no longer following her on X. It was also sponsored by Kalshi, because everything in this relationship is totally fucking cursed, dude. In her statement, Zilis wrote, “It’s hard to go from in love to let go in a week with no warning, but that’s just how it is sometimes.” Zilis, in addition to her romantic, uh, entanglement with Musk, also served as… well, she denied under oath that she was his chief of staff but says she worked across Musk’s “entire AI portfolio: Tesla, Neuralink, and OpenAI” during a trial earlier this year, in which Musk sued Sam Altman — long story, there’s some specious legal reasoning but mostly it just looks like punishment for being successful without Musk — over Musk’s donations to OpenAI. During the trial, she claimed to work 80-to-100-hour weeks for Musk, “to go find bottlenecks and solve them.” Musk apparently had a different view of her role, testifying that she was his chief of staff, and “uh, you know,” prompting loud laughter from the courtroom’s gallery. Musk has a history of public flameouts with the women who bear his children. Besides his first wife, Justine Musk, who wrote “I Was a Starter Wife” before going absolutely silent on the subject of her ex, another mother of his children, Ashley St. Clair, has said that she rejected a $40 million NDA from Musk. (She is presently suing him over his chatbot, Grok, making deepfake nudes of her.) Another ex, Grimes, referred to pregnancy as “sacrificing your body and your freedom,” and later sued him to establish a parental relationship. Grimes also posted and deleted a tweet saying “Tell Shivon to unblock me and tell Elon to let me see my son or plz respond to my lawyer” to Musk’s biographer Walter Isaacson in 2023. Musk’s fixer, Jared Birchall, orchestrates privacy deals for Musk with the baby mamas. Musk has 14 known children. Zilis was a member of OpenAI’s board when she gave birth to twins, though she kept the parentage of the children secret. She only informed her coworkers about having kids with one of their competitors in 2022, after Business Insider reported on court documents listing Musk as the children’s father. Musk lived with her at the time of the testimony. During her testimony in the case, Zilis appeared to worship Musk, and her breakup post strikes roughly the same tone. “I feel happy that I got to show Elon how it feels to be deeply understood, nurtured, and peacefully loved with stability and gentleness,” she wrote. “Given the tumultuous nature of his early life, his often tortured soul, and how hard he fights for humanity I wanted him to feel the deepest and most stable form of love this world can provide.” The post is so groveling that had I not witnessed her in court, I would have assumed this was some kind of passive-aggressive revenge strategy. Personally, if one of my exes publicly wrote that I was a poor fragile wreck trying to save the world who desperately needed a haven of safety, I would simply die of embarrassment, but God really does make all kinds. “I’ve loved him more than life itself and he’s taught me 100 lifetimes of knowledge and made my cup overflow with life meaning, so there is a lot of loss, but luckily we created four beautiful little loves of my life,” Zilis wrote. Last week, Zilis posted about a memoir written by Maye Musk, Elon’s mother: “During tough moments I think about the resilience she’s shown and realize she’s encountered 100x the difficultly I’ve faced and she made it through with grace! It gives me resolve.” I guess we know now what some of the “tough moments” were. “I would highly recommend this book to anyone who wants a beacon of resilience to draw inspiration from,” she added.

articles.title: Fox News AI Newsletter: The neighborhood on the edge of America's tech frontier
articles.summary: The Fox News AI Newsletter covers the latest artificial intelligence technology advancements, including the challenges and opportunities AI presents now and for the future.
articles.body: Welcome to Fox News’ Artificial Intelligence newsletter with the latest AI technology advancements. IN TODAY’S NEWSLETTER: - Inside the neighborhood living on the edge of America’s tech frontier - Chinese AI model investigated after researcher says it provided instructions for bioweapons, assassinations - Trump’s new high-tech government hub holds some bizarre surprises: ‘Enjoy finding them’ GRID AND BEAR IT: For homeowners on the tucked-away cul-de-sac of Statesboro Place in Loudoun County, Virginia, suburban life now shares a fence line with the infrastructure powering America's artificial intelligence (AI) boom. KILLER APP: Chinese AI company Moonshot AI has launched an internal investigation after a researcher found that one of its models could be manipulated into providing instructions for developing biological weapons and carrying out assassinations, Fox News senior foreign policy correspondent Gillian Turner reported Thursday. HIDDEN DELIGHTS: Users digging into President Donald Trump’s new AI-powered America.gov discovered a series of hidden features embedded across the federal platform, including a "Minecraft"-inspired response and a search bar that transforms into a hot dog. OPINION: The legacy media have decided we are facing mankind’s doom. The phrase "AI apocalypse" crops up on numerous news sites, from Reuters to The Economist. Other outlets have gone with "AI doomsday" or other formulations that look like they come from Revelation. COMMERCE TECH: Meta on Tuesday unveiled a version of its Muse artificial intelligence (AI) agent for small businesses. OPINION: Despite the recent surge in AI doomerism, President Donald Trump is right to maintain his strong support for data centers. As he notes: "China couldn’t be happier" if we were to turn our backs on these centers as a nation, which would effectively let the Chinese Communist Party win the AI race. OFFICIAL OVERHAUL: President Donald Trump on Tuesday signed an executive order directing the federal government to replace the term "artificial intelligence" with "Super Intelligence" across the executive branch, cementing a rebranding effort he has championed in recent weeks. DIGITAL DANGER: A Tennessee grandmother has filed a lawsuit against a North Dakota city and police department, accusing officials of wrongfully detaining her for nearly six months after allegedly misusing artificial intelligence facial recognition technology to investigate a bank theft case. OUT OF THE BOX: Nvidia on Monday announced the release of software safety tools for artificial intelligence (AI) agents that it said would've stopped the hack of Hugging Face by rogue OpenAI agents. PARTY CRASHERS: Protesters crashed a large pro-data center party in Washington, D.C., making obscene guestures attendees and shouting about the industry's water use as President Donald Trump pushes to accelerate America's artificial intelligence and data center boom.
